sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Neptune?
sections.html:
Neptune Township is a Monmouth County shore community of 8.13 square miles, and selling a house there starts with a Certificate of Inspection from Code Enforcement, which the township requires for a sale and enforces with fines.

Below you will find the Neptune numbers, the inspection checklist, tax dates, the county recording office and the three ways to sell: a listing, a sale by owner, or an as-is cash purchase.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Neptune?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 28,273 residents for July 1, 2025, only 0.4% above the 2020 base. The township had 28,061 people in 2020 and 27,935 in 2010, so it is a settled community with little change in size.

One in five residents is 65 or older, so estate sales and downsizing are a regular source of listings. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $1.37 billion in 2022, which is more than twice the township's $593 million in retail sales.

sections.h2: What are Neptune's neighborhoods and landmarks?
sections.html:
Neptune runs from the Atlantic Ocean west to Garden State Parkway Exit 100, with the Shark River estuary on the south and Asbury Park and Ocean Township on the north. Incorporated on February 26, 1879 from part of Ocean Township, it later lost land to Neptune City, Bradley Beach and, briefly, a separate Ocean Grove that was undone in 1921.

Neptune has distinct neighborhoods, and buyers shop by them. Ocean Grove is a seaside Victorian community and a national historic district of 220 acres bounded by Fletcher Lake, Route 71, Lake Wesley and the ocean, with the Camp Meeting Association dating to 1869. Shark River Hills sits along the river, Mid-Town is undergoing a township-led revitalization, and West Neptune has the Route 66 commercial strip. The Gables, Green Grove, Summerfield, Bradley Park and Seaview Island complete the neighborhood list.

  • Water covers 8.11% of the township, including Deal Lake, a 158-acre lake shared with six other towns.
  • Neighbors include Asbury Park, Avon-by-the-Sea, Belmar, Bradley Beach, Neptune City, Ocean Township, Tinton Falls and Wall Township.
  • Jersey Shore University Medical Center, a 691-bed hospital, sits in the township and anchors the local job market.

sections.h2: Which roads, trains and schools matter in Neptune?
sections.html:
Routes 18, 33, 35, 66 and 71 cross the township, and the Garden State Parkway is reached at Exits 100 and 102. The Bradley Beach station on NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line carries riders to Newark Penn, Secaucus Junction, New York Penn and Hoboken, and buses 317 (Philadelphia), 830, 832 and 836 serve local routes.

Neptune Township Schools cover pre-kindergarten through twelfth grade across seven schools: Gables, Green Grove, Midtown Community, Shark River Hills and Summerfield elementary schools, Neptune Middle School and Neptune High School. Enrollment was 3,411 in 2022-23. The district is a former Abbott district, now called an SDA district, where the state pays school construction costs.

sections.h2: Does Neptune require a Certificate of Inspection to sell a house?
sections.html:
Yes. Neptune's Code Enforcement checklist warns that buying, selling or renting a property without a Certificate of Inspection is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 and up to 90 days in jail. The township's Transfer of Title application, which carries a non-refundable $65 fee, also records that the buyer cannot occupy the home until a clear certificate is issued, with a fine up to $1,250.

The checklist sets conditions before an inspection is even scheduled: all construction permits and violations closed, taxes and sewer charges paid current, and a surrogate's certificate naming the executor if the property sits in an estate. An application has 30 days to be completed or it goes void, and the home must be vacant at inspection.

  • Exterior: house numbers at least 3 inches high, no peeling paint, gutters and downspouts in place, sound handrails and walkways, and an automated trash and recycling container left with the property.
  • Interior: smoke detectors on each level, carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas where required, GFCI outlets in kitchens and baths, and an emergency shut-off on the furnace.
  • Oil tanks no longer in use must be removed or filled, which needs a demolition permit.
  • Wood-burning fireplaces need a certified chimney sweep's letter.

Code Enforcement is at 25 Neptune Boulevard and can be reached at 732-988-5200, extension 260. The township accepts applications online through its forms page.

sections.h2: Can I rent out or short-term rent a Neptune house before selling?
sections.html:
Neptune licenses rentals separately. A standard rental application covers leases of at least one year (365 days), and a rental of a home built before 1978 needs a lead certificate or inspection. Short-term rentals use their own application with two seasons, a winter period from October 1 to May 22 and a summer period from May 23 to September 30.

If you are selling a house that has tenants, remember the township wants rental units vacant at inspection. Plan the move-out dates against your closing date, and ask Code Enforcement whether the new owner needs a rental certificate or an owner-occupancy certificate after closing.

sections.h2: When are Neptune property taxes due, and how is the assessment handled?
sections.html:
Neptune taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Interest is 8% up to $1,500 and 18% above that, and a penalty of up to 6% can apply to delinquencies over $10,000 left unpaid at year end. Sewer charges are billed separately and are due March 1 and September 1.

In 2026 the township mailed third-quarter bills on July 29 and extended that quarter's grace period from August 10 to August 24. Any municipal charge unpaid on the eleventh day of the eleventh month can go to tax sale. The Tax Collector cannot change an assessment, so errors go to the assessor, who describes a 2014 revaluation that took effect in the 2015 tax year and an annual reassessment program afterward.

Seniors and Social Security disability recipients can apply for the PAS-1 property tax relief form, and veterans' deduction forms are on the Tax Office page. Call the Tax Office at 732-988-5200, extension 251, for the exact payoff before closing.

sections.h2: How is a Neptune deed recorded in Monmouth County?
sections.html:
The Monmouth County Clerk records deeds for Neptune at its main office, Market Yard, 33 Mechanic Street in Freehold, with recording hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday and a phone line at 732-431-7324.

The clerk's fee page lists $40 for the first page of a deed and $10 for each added page, and says the transfer tax must be paid when the deed is recorded. For sales over $1 million, it points to the revised fee under P.L. 2025, c. 69 effective July 10, 2025. Confirm current figures with your attorney or title agent.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself or accept a cash offer in Neptune?
sections.html:
The Certificate of Inspection makes a plain listing slower for a house that needs work. A cash purchase is a practical fit for estate properties, tenant-occupied houses and homes with open permits, since the buyer takes the property as-is.

  • An agent listing brings the most exposure, especially in Ocean Grove and Shark River Hills.
  • A sale by owner saves the commission and keeps the paperwork with you.
  • A cash sale closes on your timeline and skips repairs, with the inspection still needed before occupancy.

Weigh each offer after the inspection costs, tax payoff and closing costs, then choose the route that fits your timeline.

faqs.q: Is a Certificate of Inspection required to sell a house in Neptune?
faqs.a: Yes. Neptune requires one for a sale, and the township's checklist lists fines up to $2,000 and up to 90 days in jail for buying, selling or renting without one. The Transfer of Title application carries a $65 fee.

faqs.q: Can a buyer move in before the Neptune inspection is done?
faqs.a: No. The Transfer of Title affidavit states the buyer will not permit occupancy until a clear Certificate of Inspection is obtained, and the township lists a fine up to $1,250 for occupying without one.

faqs.q: When are Neptune property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Interest is 8% up to $1,500 and 18% above that. Sewer charges are due March 1 and September 1.

faqs.q: What does Code Enforcement check before a Neptune sale closes?
faqs.a: It checks permits and violations, current taxes and sewer, house numbers, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, GFCI outlets, the furnace, stairs, gutters and trash containers, among other items. The full checklist is on the township's Code Enforcement pages.

faqs.q: Where is a Neptune deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Monmouth County Clerk's Office, 33 Mechanic Street, Freehold. The office records property documents Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
